name: Street Corn Chicken Rice Bowl

ingredients.buy: 2/3 cup crumbled; 1/2 cup crumbled, for topping
juice and zest of 3 1/2 limes; 7 tablespoons
1/2 cup chopped; 2/3 cup chopped; 1 1/2 cups leaves, for topping

writer_notes: All 20 locked ingredient lines are used by a step; no orphaned buys and no invented ingredients.
Sea Salt is used in two components (chicken spice mix and rice water); both fall under the single locked Sea Salt line, so it is written once in method.
Water for the rice is intentionally kept non-numeric in prose because it is not a locked or costed figure.
Cook temperature (165F) and step timings (about 20 min simmer, 4 to 5 min per side) are method details taken verbatim from the transcription, not engine macros.
cost_ps is rendered via the ${{cost_ps}} token; no per-line costs and no comparative package claims appear in shop_smart since cost_lines were not available to trace them.
Avocado, red onion and the final lime are added fresh at serving, not packed hot, to prevent browning and sogginess.

prose.intro_html:
Mexican street corn, the elote you get from a cart with lime and cotija and a little heat, is one of the great flavors on earth. The trouble is it usually shows up as a side you forget about ten minutes later. Here we build a whole dinner around it instead. Seasoned chicken, cilantro lime rice, and a cool street corn salad that does the heavy lifting.

The numbers are the reason this one earns a spot in the rotation. You get {{protein}} grams of protein per serving and it lands at {{cal}} calories, which is right where a real dinner should sit. Fourteen containers out of one afternoon of work, and every single one of them tastes like something you would actually order.
prose.shop_smart:
The chicken is the anchor. You need 4 3/4 pounds of boneless skinless breast, so reach for the big value pack rather than the little trays by the register. Cut it into 1-inch chunks yourself and you control the size and you control the price.

Corn is the star of the salad, and canned drained corn is exactly what the original calls for, so grab cans of sweet whole kernel corn and drain them well. No grill required. Same thinking on the limes: you are juicing and zesting several of them and keeping juice back for the finish, so buy them by the bag instead of one at a time.

Cotija does double duty, once folded into the corn salad and once crumbled over the top, so pick up enough to cover both jobs. If your store hides it, a firm queso fresco is the closest stand-in. Greek yogurt and mayonnaise make the dressing creamy, and a few jalapenos, a bunch of cilantro, avocados and a red onion round out the fresh side of the cart.
prose.make_it:
Start the rice, because it takes the longest. Bring a pot of water to a boil, add the rice and sea salt, cover, drop the heat to low, and simmer until tender, about 20 minutes. While it steams, stir together the chopped cilantro, fresh lime juice and lime zest in a big bowl. When the rice is done, fold it into that cilantro lime mix while it is still warm so it drinks up the flavor.

Now the street corn salad. In a bowl, combine the corn, Greek yogurt, cotija, mayonnaise, lime juice and zest, the diced jalapeno if you want the heat, chopped cilantro and salt. Stir gently until it comes together, then taste and adjust. Set it aside so the flavors can marry.

For the chicken, mix the chili powder, sea salt, cumin, smoked paprika, garlic powder and onion powder in a small bowl. Toss the chicken chunks with that seasoning until every piece is coated. Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium, add the chicken, and cook about 4 to 5 minutes per side until it is cooked through and reaches 165 degrees inside. Work in batches if your skillet is crowded, because crowded chicken steams instead of browning.

Everything is ready to build. Lay down the warm cilantro lime rice, top it with the chicken, add a generous scoop of the street corn salad, then finish with cubed avocado, sliced red onion, a little more cotija and cilantro, and a squeeze of fresh lime.
prose.portion_html:
This batch makes 14 servings, and the honest way to split it even is to weigh as you go. Cook everything, portion the rice across your 14 containers by eye first, then even it out on a kitchen scale so nobody gets shorted. Do the same with the chicken. Weighing beats guessing every time.

Rice on the bottom, chicken next, then the street corn salad tucked into its own corner so it does not soak the rice. Hold the avocado, the red onion and the final squeeze of lime until the day you eat each bowl. Avocado browns fast, and keeping the fresh toppings separate is what makes bowl number fourteen taste like bowl number one.

prose.upsell_html: If Tex-Mex bowls are your thing, this one belongs in the regular rotation right next to the taco and fajita builds. Same cook-once rhythm, same fridge-friendly payoff, a different flavor so the week never gets boring. Make a batch, tell us how the street corn salad landed, and go build the next one.
